name: Advanced Methods in STS
description: Can artistic approaches be used as a social science research method? Are they better for conveying science and technology than abstract, quantitative data? How does art, science and technology relate to each other? This blocked course offers students a mix of theoretical and methodological input to learn about and try out arts-based research methods and public engagement around science and technology. Through introductory lectures, practical exercises, a guest lecture, discussions, and a final interactive engagement format, the course will start off with an overview of how researchers in science and technology studies (STS) and related social sciences & humanities have considered and tried out artistic approaches to both critically study and convey lived realities at the intersection of science, technology, culture and society; including Art, Science and Technology Studies (ASTS), Making & Doing projects in STS, multimodal anthropology, among others. Students will learn to distinguish between instrumentalizing arts for science communication and using creative research methods to study the sociocultural dimensions of science and technology. After choosing a topic, and based on various case studies, they will experiment with creative methods and expand on their own artistic proclivities, such as visual storytelling (video and photography, drawing, Visual Vignettes, zines), mail and postcard art, sound techniques (short podcast, audio installation), speculative design, poetry and performance. For their final participatory format, students will also co-develop an evaluation framework as a critical mode of reflection. Throughout the course, participants will gain a critical understanding of how art as a method, science and technology are co-produced.
